title: A positive-degree finite unramified lci slice in a space over a field
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], and let $X$ be a nonempty algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-trf-algebraic-space], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Suppose $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. There exist an integer $d\geq1$, a scheme $Z$ finite locally free of degree $d$ over $k$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and a $k$-map $Z\to X$ which is unramified and a local complete intersection morphism in the chartwise Koszul-regular sense defined in [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]. No perfection or algebraic closedness of $k$, nor smoothness, separation, or quasi-compactness of $X$, is assumed. The field $k$ is not replaced by an extension.

source.place: Tag 06DA (lemma-lci-surjective), proof applied to a nonempty locally finitely presented algebraic space over a field.

proof.text: Choose an etale scheme atlas of $X$ and a nonempty affine open chart $V$ of that atlas. This is possible because the atlas covers the nonempty space. The structure map $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite presentation by the chartwise hypothesis; since $V$ is affine it is of finite type. Its Cohen–Macaulay locus $C$ is a nonempty open by the generic Cohen–Macaulay theorem for finite-type $k$-algebras. The Jacobson theorem supplies a point $v\in C$ closed in $V$: closed points of $V$ are dense, so they meet the nonempty open $C$. In particular $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ is Noetherian and its depth equals its dimension. The structure map is flat, since every module over a field has a basis and tensoring a vector-space injection preserves injectivity.

source.place: Tag 06DA (lemma-lci-surjective), proof: choose V and a closed Cohen–Macaulay point

proof.text: Apply the regular slicing theorem to $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the closed point $v$. Its fibre is $V$ itself, its flatness was checked in Step 1, and its fibre stalk is the Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian ring just obtained. We obtain a regular immersion $i:Z\to V$ with $Z\ne\varnothing$, $|Z|$ a singleton, and $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ flat and locally of finite presentation. Choose an affine open neighbourhood of its sole point; it is all of $Z$, since an open subscheme with full underlying open set is the whole scheme. Thus $Z$ is affine and of finite type over $k$, and its singleton space has dimension zero.

source.place: Tag 06DA (lemma-lci-surjective), proof: apply More on Morphisms Tag 0570

proof.text: Apply the finite-type dimension-zero theorem to $Z$: its structure morphism is finite. Together with the flatness and local finite presentation from Step 2, this is finite locally free. Write $Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$; finiteness means that $B$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space. Set $d=\dim_k B$. Since $Z$ has a point, $B\ne0$, so $d\ge1$. The sole fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $Z$ itself; hence its dimension of global sections is $d$, exactly the degree condition in the definition.

source.place: Tag 06DA (lemma-lci-surjective), proof: finite and then finite locally free of positive degree

proof.text: The immersion $i$ is unramified directly from the scheme definition: locally it is a quotient of rings followed by an open inclusion, hence is locally of finite type and a monomorphism; its diagonal is an isomorphism onto $Z\times_VZ$, therefore an open immersion. The etale map $e:V\to X$ is unramified, and the space-composition theorem makes $e\circ i$ unramified.

source.place: Tag 06DA (lemma-lci-surjective), proof: unramifiedness of the composite

proof.text: Regularity of $i$ means that near each source point its closed-immersion factor has ideal generated by a regular sequence. Such a sequence is Koszul-regular by the regular-to-Koszul theorem. Its other factor is an open immersion, hence smooth: an affine infinitesimal lifting problem factors through the open exactly when its underlying topological image does, and a nilpotent thickening does not change that image; open restrictions are locally finitely presented. Therefore this is a factorization witnessing the chartwise lci condition. The etale map $e$ is lci by the space-lci theorem, and its composition with $i$ is lci by that same theorem. Both maps and the composite are over $k$, so the finite locally free $Z$ and $d$ from Step 3 give the required slice over the original field.

source.place: Tag 06DA (lemma-lci-surjective), proof: regular immersion is lci and compose with the etale chart

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NW-f11275410 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The delivery follows Stacks 06DA (criteria.tex, lemma-lci-surjective) step by step, and I checked each step against the statements it cites. Step 1: a nonempty affine chart V of finite type over k; the Cohen–Macaulay locus is dense open (lem-trf-generic-cm-locus-field = 00RG); the Jacobson node gives a closed point in it; flatness over a field is elementary. Step 2: the new 0570 slice node applies with every hypothesis checked, so Z is a single point and therefore affine of dimension 0. Step 3: 06LH finiteness gives finite locally free of degree d=dim_k B, which is at least 1. Step 4: an immersion is unramified directly from the definition, and lem-sfb-space-unramified-permanence covers etale and composition. Step 5: a regular sequence is Koszul-regular, an open immersion is smooth, and the new lci node gives etale-lci and composition (06C8). The item statement is unchanged, agrees with 06DA's field claim and is not weakened. There is no cycle and proof_deps equals the union of the uses. New nodes: the regular slice keeps the regularity that lem-trf-cm-closed-point-flat-quasifinite-slice drops, and the lci-composition node (06C8/06C9) is true. Neither is a duplicate: I checked them against 06LI, 06LW, 0571, 06CE, the source-locus node, the syntomic node and the trf lci nodes. FIX: the slice node's regularity clause cited a ring-level regular sequence on an arbitrary open subscheme, which is not meaningful there. I restated it affine-locally in Stacks' form (Z' ≅ Spec(A/I) in an affine open Spec A, with I generated by an A-regular sequence, r=0 allowed), made 'Z→S' the composite f∘i, and added def-weil-affine-spectrum and def-weil-open-immersion to stmt_deps. I tested it on k[x,y]/(xy), the affine line over k at a closed point, k[ε], and the affine line over Z_p at (p,t). Batch-5 flags: lem-trf-generic-cm-locus-field is generic commutative algebra (00RG), and the other three flags reach the trace-formula chapter only through the general definition def-trf-algebraic-space. All are outside the trace-formula and Poincaré-duality statements and their proofs, so I accept them. I accept the four declared tool_uses as generic. No SGA source is used.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
